name: Hagley Museum
unique: The du Pont gunpowder works on the Brandywine, with water powered mills you walk through, a powder yard demonstration that shakes the valley and the family mansion.
buzz: The explosion demonstration is the reason children agree to the museum; the walk along the raceway is beautiful and mostly shaded.

name: Winterthur Museum
unique: Henry du Pont's 175-room mansion holding the world's premier collection of American decorative arts, set in 60 acres of naturalistic garden.
buzz: The period rooms are jaw-dropping; the garden tram is the sleeper hit. Some find the guided only format slow.

name: Fort Delaware
unique: A moat ringed Civil War fortress on an island in the Delaware River, reached by ferry, with prison barracks, tunnels and a living history garrison.
buzz: The ferry and the moat make it an adventure; the prison history is grim and well told. Bring lunch, there is nothing on the island.

name: Air Mobility Command Museum
unique: A hangar of C-5s, C-141s and a C-47 restored as a D-Day aircraft, plus the only B-17 in Delaware, free and walk around open.
buzz: Volunteers are often retired loadmasters and will open cockpits; the C-5 is the size people cannot get over.

name: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Sixteen thousand acres of tidal salt marsh and impoundments on the Delaware Bay where hundreds of thousands of shorebirds stop in May and eagles nest within sight of the road.
buzz: The auto tour loop is the way in and the observation tower at Raymond Pool is where the photographers set up; bring bug spray in summer.

name: Dogfish Head Brewery Tour
unique: The brewery that invented continual hopping and put American craft beer on the map, with a tour that includes the original 1995 brewhouse and a tasting.
buzz: Tours are praised for honesty about failures and for generous pours; book ahead and eat at the brewpub.

name: Nemours Estate
unique: A 77-room French neoclassical mansion built by Alfred du Pont, with formal gardens modeled on Versailles and a garage full of vintage cars.
buzz: Less crowded than the du Pont mansions in Pennsylvania; reviews praise the gardens and the car collection.

name: Cape Henlopen and Fort Miles
unique: A WWII coastal defense fort with a concrete observation tower you can climb, plus dunes, bay beach and ocean beach in one park.
buzz: The tower tour is the reason to come; the beaches are quieter than Rehoboth. Bikes are the best way around.

name: Dover Motor Speedway
unique: A mile concrete oval known as the Monster Mile, with banking that lets you see the whole field from the frontstretch and a campground that becomes a small city.
buzz: Fans say the concrete makes the racing better and the traffic easier than the big tracks; the September race is the traditional weekend.

name: Delaware Art Museum
unique: The largest collection of Pre-Raphaelite art in the country outside Britain, in a bank building on a wooded park, with a strong Howard Pyle illustration collection.
buzz: The Pre-Raphaelites are the surprise and the American illustration galleries the local pride; it is a two hour museum and free on Sundays.

name: Rehoboth Beach Boardwalk
unique: A mile of boardwalk with a 1920s merry-go-round, Thrasher's fries in vinegar and a beach town that still shuts its bars early.
buzz: It is the Mid-Atlantic's cleanest family beach; parking is the eternal complaint. Go in September.

name: Bethany Beach Boardwalk
unique: A quiet half mile boardwalk with a bandstand, a totem pole and a beach that is calmer than Rehoboth's, in a town that bans alcohol on the sand.
buzz: Families choose it for the calm water and the quiet; the boardwalk is a walk, not a carnival, and parking is free but tight.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park
unique: A barrier beach between the ocean and Rehoboth Bay, with a surfing beach on the inlet side, a fishing pier and a campground under the bridge.
buzz: The inlet is where the surf is consistent and the bay side is flat for kayaks; the bridge traffic in summer is the local joke.
